shared_qualifications: C1: V(SCE)*1000=mV(SCE), with no reference offset. The source5Mo and pure-Cr results explicitly show no pitting up to transpassive dissolution at approximately+0.85 V. A censored pitting lower limit is not an observed pitting onset or a numerical conversion of transpassivity.

C2: source potential increments are25 mV with a1 min dwell (PDF p.3), giving a nominal25/60=0.416667 mV/s; CRA0.417 is not proof of a continuous sweep. Source1 N HCl is deaerated,25 C, pH0.02, versus CRA pH0.0. The inspected source uses heat treatment1050 C/2 h and water quenching (PDF p.2); CRA heat cells are blank.

The source20Cr-25Ni-5Mo formula is nominal; Table I analysis is Cr19.96/Ni25.66/Mo5.06 wt%. CRA179 uses that analysis, while183/201 use nominalCr20/Ni25/Mo5. These are retained as alternative representations, not automatically collapsed as duplicate runs. Their numerical850/880 targets do not establish counterpart identity for the registered no-pitting bound.

Only the source explicitly stated17Cr-25Ni-5Mo pitting onset above approximately0.40 V is supported as a numerical threshold counterpart. Other unregistered continuous curves were not converted into new observations.
